input.quote: (a) At any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding, either party may terminate this Agreement for any or no reason upon fifteen (15) days advance notice to the other.
input.rationale: The term is evergreen (§ 2: continues until terminated under § 6), and the only convenience right (§ 6(a)) is available solely "at any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding." We therefore have no convenience exit from any active engagement, and § 6(b) is limited to material breach — this fails the fallback, which requires a Customer convenience right (30–90 days' notice) without penalty. The Vendor side is acceptable: Contractor likewise cannot walk away while a Statement of Work is outstanding, so the 15-day mutual right operates only between engagements and needs no change. Redline adds a new § 6(c) giving Company a 30 days' notice convenience right with Contractor paid for Services performed and a refund of prepaid, unearned fees; 60 days' notice is offered as a fallback.

proposal.summary: Add Company right to terminate the Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience on 30 days' notice with refund of prepaid, unearned fees
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 6(a) only permits convenience termination when no Statement of Work is outstanding, so on an evergreen term we would be locked into every engagement; we have added a Company right to terminate the Agreement or any Statement of Work on thirty (30) days' notice with a refund of prepaid, unearned fees, with Contractor paid for Services performed through termination. If 30 days is difficult we can move to 60 days' notice.

ops.text: (c) In addition, Company may terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days advance written notice to Contractor, without penalty or early-termination charge. Upon any such termination, Contractor will be paid all fees and expenses incurred or earned for Services properly performed through the effective date of termination, and Contractor shall refund to Company any prepaid fees for Services not performed as of that date.
